findings.title: #StopRansomware: Gunra Ransomware (AA26-222A)
findings.summary_md: CISA, FBI, NSA, DC3, USSS, and South Korea's KNPA released a joint advisory on Aug 10, 2026 describing Gunra ransomware affiliates exploiting CVE-2024-55591 and CVE-2025-24472 in exposed FortiOS/FortiProxy appliances, along with SSH/credential weaknesses in public-facing VPN gateways. The advisory covers the group's double-extortion model, Linux variant weakness (predictable srand seed), IoCs, MITRE ATT&CK mappings, and mitigation steps including network segmentation and offline backups.

findings.title: Gunra Ransomware Group Unveils Efficient Linux Variant
findings.summary_md: Trend Micro reported on Jul 29, 2025 that Gunra's Linux variant uses up to 100 parallel encryption threads with partial-encryption control, targets Windows and Linux, and drops the .ENCRT extension. The group first appeared in April 2025, has victimized organizations across Brazil, Japan, Canada, Turkey, South Korea, Taiwan, and the U.S., and operates a Tor-based data-leak site. The blog notes 14 claimed victims and provides IOCs and hunting queries for Trend Vision One.

findings.title: Fortinet PSIRT Advisory FG-IR-24-535 (CVE-2024-55591 / CVE-2025-24472)
findings.summary_md: Fortinet published FG-IR-24-535 on Jan 14, 2025 confirming active exploitation of an authentication-bypass vulnerability (CVE-2024-55591, CVSS 9.6) affecting FortiOS 7.0.0-7.0.16 and FortiProxy 7.2.0-7.2.12, expanded on Feb 11, 2025 to include CVE-2025-24472. The advisory details attacker-created admin accounts (random usernames, super-admin privileges), malicious SSL-VPN user groups, IoC log patterns, affected versions, upgrade paths (FortiOS 7.0.17+, FortiProxy 7.2.13+), and workarounds restricting administrative access.
